title: SAGE Edge Inference Configuration
description: Defines tier assignments and inference rules for automatic graph edge creation during ingestion. Three tiers based on cost of false positives. Staging table isolates suggested edges (Tier 2) from the production graph. See SAGE Architecture Reference Section 3.4.7.

tier_assignments.description: Maps edge types to inference tiers with optional inference rules. Every edge type in the vault's edge taxonomy should have an assignment. Unassigned edge types default to Tier 3 (manual only).

edge_type.description: The edge type being assigned to a tier. Must be a member of the EdgeType enum in the SAGE Core API; resolution_policy for each edge type is declared separately in the vault's edge_type_registry (CAS-ADR-017).

tier.description: Inference tier. 1: auto-create (deterministic, no review). 2: auto-suggest (placed in staging table for batch review). 3: manual only (requires human or agent judgment).

inference_rules.description: Rules for how this edge type is inferred during ingestion. Required for Tier 1 and Tier 2 assignments. Not applicable for Tier 3.

method.description: Inference method. version_chain: filename version numbers (v15 supersedes v14 through v1); chain identity is (title, project, doc_type), so documents with different doc_types do not chain even if they share a title. re_ingestion: change detection triggered re-ingestion. filename_code_match: target document code appears in this document's filename. filename_co_location: documents share a code and workflow stage. content_reference: textual cross-references within document content (placeholder; superseded by identifier_mention). identifier_mention (T-0016): verbatim canonical-identifier mentions in the ingested document's projected body text resolve to vault-resident targets via tag and title-prefix lookups; pattern set is declared in the `patterns` array on the inference rule.

pattern.description: For filename-based methods: a pattern or regex describing how to identify the relationship from filename segments. For content_reference: a pattern describing what to look for in content. Not used by identifier_mention (which uses the structured `patterns` array instead).

patterns.description: Identifier patterns for the identifier_mention method. Each pattern declares an identifier regex and the tag/tier3/title/doc_type filters used to resolve the matched literal to a vault document. At least one of `target_tags` or `target_tier3` must be declared to scope the resolver away from a doc_type-wide lookup. T-0016, T-0139.

regex.description: Python regex matched verbatim against the ingested document's projected body text. Should include word boundaries (e.g., `\bCAS-ADR-\d{3}\b`) to avoid spurious mid-word matches. The matched literal is fed to the resolver as the identifier.

target_tags.description: Tags the resolved target document must carry. May contain `{id}` as a placeholder for the matched identifier literal (e.g., `id:{id}` resolves to `id:T-0016` for a `T-0016` mention). All tags AND together. Mutually exclusive in practice with `target_tier3`, but the schema permits combining them; both filters AND together at query time.

target_tier3.description: Tier-3 metadata fields (CAS-ADR-028) the resolved target document's `tier3_metadata` dict must carry as exact-match values. Each value may contain `{id}` as a placeholder for the matched identifier literal (e.g., `{ticket_id: "{id}"}` resolves to `ticket_id=T-0042` for a `T-0042` mention). All pairs AND together. Used for doc_types whose canonical identity lives in `tier3_metadata` rather than tags. T-0139.

target_title_prefix.description: Optional title-prefix filter applied after tag/tier3 filtering. May contain `{id}` as a placeholder. Used for ADR-style identifiers where the tag is generic (`adr`) but title carries the id prefix (e.g., `ADR-{adr_num}:`).

enabled.description: Set to false to disable this pattern without removing it from config.

source_segment.description: The filename segment on the source document that participates in the match.

target_segment.description: The filename segment on the target document that participates in the match.

staging_review_grouping.description: How Tier 2 suggested edges are grouped for batch review in the human application.
